task: Core #1186 F6-U03g: PostgreSQL17 exact positive and negative table lock/catalog row guard fixture (hosted disabled)

assuranceCeiling.rationale: Critical-risk source-to-runtime gap: exercise 177 ordered table locks and seven allowed catalog hashes on real, isolated PG17 with good and bad data, contention and rollback; retain separate hosted authority boundary.

acceptanceCriteria: Real PostgreSQL17 service confirms 177 fixture relations and full 113 synthetic permitted catalog records in 7 tables, plus zero user data in all other fixture tables.
Real transaction-local guard passes on unchanged positive state, fails on one-row mutation, unauthorized customer row, missing/extra relation and NOWAIT conflict without leaving partial writes.
Atomic guard and source unit tests prove a fixed container-bound loopback server with no libpq/environment redirect and no use of Supabase credentials.
Proof output declares LOCAL_SYNTHETIC_177_TABLES_ONLY, production 4621-object and hosted 59-file migrations unproved; original F6-U03b unconditional abort remains.
All exact-head standard CI, TypeScript, full quality tests, Completion Truth and Lifecycle successfully close a scoped unit before a next Core task starts.
invariants: Only f6u03g_* test schemas, fixture tables and synthetic metadata are ever created or locked by this unit.
Total 177 fixture application relations and seven 113-row neutral catalogs must not be mistaken for identity of real hosted application schema.
Contended lock, invalid count, hash drift and user data drift fail-closed before any destructive hosted SQL.
Tests that skip Postgres or fall back to mocked executors cannot satisfy runtime proof.
No repository change enables Cloud Fresh Install reset nor merges stacked Core PRs.
forbiddenStates: Any hosted Supabase credential or variable is consumed by PG fixture runner.
Any failure exits successfully while an unauthorized fixture business row or catalog mutation is present.
A NOWAIT lock conflict waits and silently passes.
Positive fixture status claims 59 customer migrations were applied to hosted Supabase.
Any modification in public/private/auth/storage hosted schemas occurs from F6-U03g.

failureModes: Catalog hash check counts rows only and misses changed record content.
Off-by-one fixture table enumeration falsely accepts 176 or 178 relations.
Business row appears in a non-neutral table but is accepted.
Separate sessions race during verification and locks do not protect application tables.
An insecure command accidentally points PostgreSQL tooling at the hosted database.
After an error, a partial destructive transaction or silent error handling is committed.
Tests overclaim synthetic fixture evidence as actual 4621 historical schema and provider readiness.
edgeCases: Seven neutral catalogs of differing 2/4/5/7/38/53-row cardinalities add to 113.
Tamper one existing catalog row value without modifying its count.
Additional business row in the final private table.
Drop or add one table after setup; count must differ from expected 177.
Two simultaneous sessions: one holds ACCESS SHARE, guard ACCESS EXCLUSIVE NOWAIT must fail immediately.
Clean positive transaction uses a newly acquired connection and proves all hashes and lock order.
Postgres17 container forwards loopback listener but server-internal IP differs: verify actual Docker service identity.
An error inside DO triggers transaction rollback and previous data is still visible from a fresh connection.

specialistReviews.finding: Fixture SQL access to postgres could be redirected via inherited libpq settings.
specialistReviews.resolution: Pin exact disposable container IP, DB and role; reject env selectors, no hosted secret in workflow.

specialistReviews.finding: Equal row counts can hide mutation and concurrent writes.
specialistReviews.resolution: Compare stable content hashes for seven catalogs and lock every application table within same transaction.

specialistReviews.finding: A synthetic 177-table pass might be mistaken for hosted Fresh Install acceptance.
specialistReviews.resolution: Publish explicit limited-scope report and keep F6-U03b abort barrier untouched.

specialistReviews.finding: Adding new proof workflows could bypass standard Core dependency order.
specialistReviews.resolution: Stack draft on F6-U03f and reuse canonical Development Guard/Plan Before Code/Completion Truth without changes to main.

challenge.scenario: Positive check only validates relation count, not seven real table records.
challenge.finding: A changed entitlement might pass if only cardinality is checked.
challenge.resolution: Compute each ordered whole-row JSONB digest in a read-only snapshot, pin baseline fixture hashes and compare on each locked transaction.

challenge.scenario: A customer row exists in a sample non-neutral table.
challenge.finding: A clean disposable database claim would be false.
challenge.resolution: Reject any non-neutral table count greater than zero; test fixture row injection.

challenge.scenario: Another client holds an ACCESS SHARE lock.
challenge.finding: An unbounded exclusive lock attempt could stall hosted users.
challenge.resolution: Use NOWAIT and a bounded statement_timeout; verify immediate error from genuinely separate PostgreSQL sessions.

challenge.scenario: A missing or extra table is silently skipped.
challenge.finding: Order or cardinality check could fail open.
challenge.resolution: Assert exact 175+2 counts and explicit seven names; test both missing and extra relations.

challenge.scenario: The test CI job uses ambient PGPASSWORD/PGHOSTADDR directing SQL to a live project.
challenge.resolution: Reject any ambient PG* or database URL selectors, construct minimal environment and validate exact service IP/database/role/major before fixture setup.

challenge.scenario: Different JSON representations create spurious digest disagreements.
challenge.finding: Digest must be stable across reads and independent of insertion order.
challenge.resolution: Use deterministic ORDER BY to_jsonb(x)::text for real fixture baseline and guard; test non-count tampering explicitly.

challenge.scenario: A failed guard returns zero exit code and the trial is incorrectly marked PASS.
challenge.finding: Mismatched state must result in a real SQL nonzero error.
challenge.resolution: Use psql -X ON_ERROR_STOP=1 and explicitly assert SQL error marker and preserved rows before returning proof.

challenge.scenario: Test result is promoted to proof of original historical DDL and provider-managed callbacks.
challenge.finding: Synthetic fixture does not cover actual 4621-object definition source.
challenge.resolution: Publish LOCAL_SYNTHETIC_177_TABLES_ONLY and mark production object fingerprint and hosted migration proof false.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: F6-U03f shipped a fail-closed source-only 177-table, seven-neutral-catalog and managed-reference transaction guard, but only a mismatched one-table Postgres17 fixture proved rejection. F6-U03g must prove positive success and precise negative outcomes for 177 relation locks and all 113 synthetic allowed catalog rows in a real isolated PostgreSQL17 fixture, without presenting mock historical catalog objects as real Supabase state or activating hosted SQL.
observableOutcomes: Exact ephemeral PostgreSQL17 CI server confirms 175+2 fixture relations, seven explicitly enumerated neutral tables totaling 113 synthetic rows and a full exclusive NOWAIT lock pass while no other application user tables contain rows.

An in-transaction DO guard verifies count and exact content hashes of all synthetic neutral tables while holding transaction-scoped locks, rejects changed catalog rows, rejects unauthorized business rows and rejects missing/extra relation schema.
Concurrent transaction holds a fixture application-table lock; guard must fail immediately with lock error and leave all previous rows unchanged.
Positive fixture guard completes its transaction and an independent session verifies unchanged baseline state; fixture errors roll back without granting authorization to any hosted reset.
Full 59-file real customer baseline application, 4621-item historical object fingerprint and provider-managed Auth/Storage grants remain unproved in this fixture and explicitly BLOCKED.
unresolvedRisks: The generated fixture is structurally analogous to 177 application relations, but lacks 4621 exact historical object definitions, original RLS/policies, original 59 migrations, managed Auth/Storage and six Supabase event triggers.
Successful DO lock verification on local CI cannot identify a Supabase TLS endpoint or prove that Auth/Storage are quiescent.
Exclusive DDL locks alone do not lock provider-managed Auth or Storage; live project proof requires independent service quiescence and rechecks.
Committed or rolled-back local fixture success cannot authorize source compiler's hard abort removal.

in: Implement minimal, deterministic 177-table local fixture with seven neutral catalogs matching historical table names and synthetically generated 113 rows, one private representative pair, no external URLs or credentials.
Implement transaction-local lock, count, per-row hash and exact-name comparison on that fixture and execute inside a real PostgreSQL17 CI service.
Run positive real guard and negative one-row catalog tamper, unauthorized sample business data, missing/extra relation count and concurrent lock denial with after-error state proof.
Prove runner rejects inherited PostgreSQL or hosted selectors, verifies exact immutable test DB/role/docker container IP before any fixture DDL.
Leave F6-U03f production candidate unchanged, preserve unconditional abort and record limited-scope evidence in the normal Shoperation CI/Lifecycle chain.
out: No hosted Supabase SQL, reset, migration replay or activation of staging.
No claims about historical 4621 object fingerprint or existing 59 reviewed SQL migrations from the fixture.
No modifications to F6-U03f execution guard or existing customer-baseline source files.
No Builder/Factory work, no new Control Plane or store runtime.
